summary: Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. He held posts at Florida International University from 1991 to 1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

Boris Turayev (1868–1920) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891). He taught Otto Neugebauer and George de Roerich, holding posts at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1896–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1922–1928) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1928–1933).

Boris Vladimirtsov (1884–1931) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at St. Petersburg University (~1904–1909) and under Antoine Meillet (~1911–1912), later serving at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1915–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).

Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Shri Singha Shedra and under Tubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam. He taught Khenpo Chökhyap, Khenpo Dazer, Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, Tarthang Tulku, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Brad Warner (born 1964) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kent State University and under Tim McCarthy, Gyomay Kubose, and Gudō Wafu Nishijima. He served as leader at Dogen Sangha International in 2007 and founded Dogen Sangha Los Angeles in 2012.

Bradford Lyman Phillips works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, the University of Virginia (BA 1989, PhD 2004), and Harvard University (MTS 1993), under Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, Jeffrey Hopkins, and doctoral supervisor David Germano.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He has held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972), department head at Jiwaji University (1970–1975), and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology and history. He completed a PhD at Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and a habilitation at Munich (2013), holding posts at SOAS (~2006–2010), Munich (~2010–2017), and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (2002).
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Louisville under the supervision of Patrick Arthur Pranke (attested 2015).

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) worked in Indology and history. He studied at Calcutta, Cambridge, and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, Harold Walter Bailey, and others. He later served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998) and taught Miranda Shaw.

Brendan S. Gillon is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He served as an associate professor in the Department of Linguistics at McGill University (~1992).

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, held teaching and research posts at Kwansei Gakuin, Shiga, Kyoto, and Otani universities, and served as Assistant (attested 2007) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2018) at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Ngawang Wangyal (~1968–1983).

Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under mentor Willis Stoesz. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and at Bates College (~2018) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor and Asian Studies Program chair.

Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history who studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, Temple, and Eihei-ji. He held posts at Auckland (~1993–2005), Adelaide (~2005–2012), Antioch (2005–2013), and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (2013).
Brian Gregory Baumann works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under the supervision of György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. After studying at East India Company College and Fort William College, he served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (1833–1843).
